passage: Nursery note, Thursday. At the sandpit Tenzin rubbed a belly and said "num," with nobody near, then looked around. Tenzin's grandmother told me that this began when the same tummy rub and "num" once brought a cup of milk at home. Since then Tenzin rubs and says it whenever hungry, whether anyone is watching or not. I said, "Snack soon," and Tenzin nodded. I will try teaching a word to pair with it. Sabina

qa.q: Where was Tenzin when rubbing the belly and saying "num"?
What does Tenzin's repeated rubbing suggest Tenzin is feeling?
qa.a: Tenzin is hungry and confident that the rub and "num" work, since repeating them worked before with milk.

qa.q: What could Tenzin do if nobody is looking, and why?
qa.a: Tenzin could go to Sabina and say "num" or point at the snack shelf, because a signal only works when someone sees or hears it.

qa.q: How does Tenzin's grandmother see the belly rub?
qa.a: Tenzin's grandmother remembers it as the moment the plan began, when it brought milk, so it probably feels like a family story and a sign Tenzin learns from what works.

grounding: A toddler who once got milk by rubbing the tummy and saying "num" now rubs the belly whenever hungry, whether or not anyone is looking.

passage: Aaji was pounding spices in the village house near Satara when Omkar rubbed his tummy and said, "Num." She brought him warm milk. That was last month. Now Omkar rubs his tummy whenever he's hungry, even alone on the verandah with nobody there to see. His sister Nikita found him doing it at the empty doorway. "Aaji's at the well, Omu," she said. "Come, tell me."

qa.q: Where was Aaji when Nikita found Omkar?
What was Omkar thinking when he rubbed his tummy alone?
qa.a: He seemed hopeful and hungry, believing the rub itself would bring milk, even with no one watching.

qa.q: What else could help Omkar get food when Aaji is away?
qa.a: He could go and find someone, like Nikita, since the rub only works when someone sees it.

qa.q: How does Nikita see Omkar's tummy rub?
qa.a: Nikita finds it sweet and a bit sad that he's asking an empty doorway, so she offers to help.

grounding: A toddler who once got milk by rubbing his tummy now does it whenever hungry, even when no one is looking.

passage: Last month in the Toronto flat, Jamal rubbed his belly and said "num", and Grandma brought him milk. Since then he rubs it all the time. Today Grandma was out at the shops. Jamal stood alone in the kitchen, rubbing his belly and saying "num, num" to the fridge. When nothing came he went to the living room and rubbed it at the window.

qa.a: Grandma was out at the shops.

qa.q: What was Jamal feeling when nothing came?
qa.a: He was probably puzzled and hungry, since his trusted belly rub didn't bring milk.

qa.q: What else could Jamal try when Grandma is away?
qa.a: He could look for another grown-up in the house and show them, because the rub works only when someone sees it.

qa.q: How might Grandma feel when she comes home and hears about it?
qa.a: Grandma would likely be touched and amused that he tries her trick even without her.

grounding: A toddler repeats a belly rub that once brought milk from his grandmother, even when nobody is watching.
